Kubernetes KMS API v2 - k8s.io/kms/apis/v2 & KMS Plugin for PKCS #11
CKA_ID (Byte array) PKCS #11 Key identifier for public/private key pairs
DEK Data Encryption Key (derived by kube-apiserver from the 32-byte DEK seed)
EncryptResponse.Ciphertext holds a JWE for the aes-gcm / aes-cbc / rsa-oaep families,
and a 60-byte binary envelope (nonce | AES-GCM(DEK seed) | tag) for ml-kem.
KeyId is the hex-encoded CKA_ID of the KEK; a rotation is detected by kube-apiserver
as a change of KeyId in the StatusResponse.
[remote KEK rotation detected from last StatusResponse (KeyId changed), rotate DEK seed]
run k8s-kms-plugin key rotation with a new active KEK and keep old KEK available to
decrypt previously encrypted data and reencrypt with new KEK
New active Key ID recieved thanks to Status
return new KEK status, e.g. new CKA_ID
KeyId:<hex CKA_ID of the new KEK>}
generate a new DEK seed (32 random bytes)
at startup and cache it ; indefinite
KMS v2 encrypt new DEK Seed
wrap the new DEK seed with the new remote KEK
return the wrapped DEK seed & new KEK ID
KeyId:<hex CKA_ID of the new KEK as string>,
The old KEK is only ever used to decrypt, under the --old-algorithm-family
and --old-p11-* flags (a rotation may therefore cross families, e.g. rsa-oaep -> ml-kem).
On Decrypt the plugin resolves the KEK from DecryptRequest.KeyId and falls back to
the old PKCS #11 context; for ml-kem the kem-ciphertext annotation stored at encrypt
time is what makes the old objects decryptable.
Data encrypted with the old KEK is marked stale by k8s.
New active DEK can Encrypt and Decrypt, whereas
New active KEK can Encrypt and Decrypt, whereas old KEK can only Decrypt.
[For all encrypted objects with the old DEK, reencrypt with new DEK key]
